dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything of note nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Well, you'd be hard-pressed to find something that isn't noteworthy in a military encampment, I reckon.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: My only concern now is to forge the weapons I am charged with well. I care little for the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Hello there, traveler from afar. If you are here to see me, does that mean that you are interested in the swords and blades of Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you, again?

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: I am a swordsmith from Tatarasuna and a successor of the Miyazaki Art.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: I have been under the protection of the Sangonomiya troops ever since the war broke out. Therefore, I decided to join them and offer them support in terms of weapons and equipment.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: If you want to ask about the forging secrets of the Miyazaki Art, I'm afraid that I can't tell you. But if you want to learn about the history around here on the other hand, I have some tales to tell.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: I have been around for long enough, after all, to know a little more than others. Hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Goodbye. Watch out for your safety around here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me more about Kannazuka?

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Kannazuka is disputed territory between the Shogunate and Sangonomiya. Actually, that place belongs neither to the Shogunate who worship the Raiden Shogun, nor to Sangonomiya, who worships Orobaxi.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: That's why this place is called Kannazuka, which means "the hill where no gods reside."

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: At Kannazuka, if you walk past the camp in the east and head southwest, you will find yourself in Tatarasuna.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you can tell me about Yashiori Island?

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: You have probably already been to the places around the Sangonomiya camp, right? If you go further south, there are some places of interest on the other side of the Musoujin Gorge. I wouldn't recommend going there though.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Inside Higi Village across the valley, I heard that the villagers have caught some strange illness. Those who could flee already have. The remaining bunch have all gone quite mad.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: It's probably because the village lies too close to the remains of gods and demons, so they were haunted by the Tatarigami.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: I heard a god's power will still linger around even if they have already been slain... So for your own sake, don't go further south.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's this Orobaxi I've been hearing about...

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: The residents of Watatsumi Island worship Orobaxi, a dragon-like serpent god who guided them back in the day.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Orobaxi taught them how to farm and how to smelt. Therefore, the people of Watatsumi Island are very grateful towards Orobaxi, worshipping it as their guardian deity.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Later on, a great battle broke out between Orobaxi and the Electro Archon, and Orobaxi was slain in that conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Fort Mumei was left in the ruined state we see today because of that battle. And the Musoujin Gorge next to it was a scar left by the Electro Archon when she delivered a blow from her Musou no Hitotachi, slaying the serpent.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Until now, Orobaxi's remains can still be seen on Yashiori Island. Those giant snake bones are the remnants of that god.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to hear about Tatarasuna...

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: The Mikage Furnace there is infused with technology from Fontaine. It is the smelting center of Inazuma. Before the incident happened, I worked over there.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: There is an island called Nazuchi Beach to the west of Tatarasuna. It is part of Yashiori Island.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Nazuchi Beach is also a chaotic place plagued by war. There are even some pirates who managed to set up their lair over there during the tumult. If you can't handle yourself well, it is very dangerous to go that way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the situation on Yashiori Island...

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Hmph. I'd only recently heard of that myself.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Although I don't know the exact details...

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: But I do know a thing or ten about those young idiots on Watatsumi Island!

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: They learned nothing of Watatsumi's legacy, even going out and doing such a disgraceful thing!

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: *sigh* If the Watatsumi Omikami praised in our songs heard of their terrible deeds, surely he too would weep in anger and grief...

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Watatsumi has suffered great humiliation under the rule of the Shogunate, yes... But paying back blood with blood was not Omikami's way.

dialogues.speaker: Miyazaki Saburou
dialogues.text: Thankfully, Her Excellency stopped those radicals in time. I only hope that they will learn their lesson and grow up...
